Cimetidine, in turn, is associated with Duodenal Ulcer (disease) via its therapeutic role in reducing gastric acid secretion. This creates a plausible pathway where Sucralfate, though not directly indicated for duodenal ulcers, may contribute to ulcer development through indirect mechanisms, possibly by influencing gastric acid secretion or mucosal protection, which are targets of Cimetidine. The evidence is supported by a consistent chain of indications and off-label use, suggesting a possible mechanistic link, though the exact role of Sucralfate remains unclear. The relationship is further strengthened by the shared therapeutic target of Cimetidine, which implies a potential overlap in mechanisms, though the direct involvement of Sucralfate in duodenal ulceration remains speculative.
